**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Regenerate the manifest after the final file changes**

Regenerate this manifest from the final candidate: the recorded SHA-256 for `README.md` is `ed57…`, while the committed file hashes to `73ff…`; the entries for `docs/TRUST_HARDENING_2026-10-14.md`, `web/app/how-ai-works/page.tsx`, and `web/app/login/page.tsx` are also stale, and the changed `me`, `talk`, and `welcome` pages are omitted. Anyone using this artifact to bind the reported checks to the reviewed candidate will therefore reject valid files or verify an incomplete snapshot.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Use a valid telephone URI for the crisis call**

When a user taps the crisis call link, `tel:988?oai_link_source=model_response_hotline` is outside the `tel:` URI grammar, which permits telephone parameters separated with semicolons rather than an HTTP-style query; handset handling of this malformed target is platform-dependent and may reject or misinterpret the number. Because this is the primary crisis call action, use a plain dialing target such as `tel:988` and keep attribution on the HTTPS link instead. See the [RFC 3966 telephone URI syntax](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc3966/).

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve support routing for delayed intent**

These new negation patterns suppress any matching risk phrase even when the rest of the clause makes the intent affirmative but delayed: for example, `I won't kill myself until tonight` and `I will not harm myself before I say goodbye` now both return `NORMAL`, whereas the previous high-risk patterns routed them to support. A present marker such as “tonight” cannot recover the match because `_clause_has_unnegated_risk` rejects negated spans before considering `present`; constrain these denials so temporal qualifiers do not turn explicit future intent into a normal chat.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Whitelist the Supabase origin embedded in the frontend**

When `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` is set independently from `SUPABASE_URL`, which `scripts/build_vercel_web.py` explicitly permits, the compiled browser client connects to the former but this CSP allows only `settings.supabase_url`. If those origins differ—for example when the browser uses a custom Supabase domain—`connect-src` blocks all authentication requests and sign-in becomes unusable; build the policy from the frontend's actual public origin or safely include both configured origins.
